I just wanted to point it out for those who have this option so they can get the most out of it. We also most likely won't have the same exact specs since some have different cpus and motherboards, but this was the results I got. None of the above mentioned FSR or Fluid motion stuff was touched in the process. Just a simple flick of a switch and it now runs every game I own like a dream.

Just so we're all aware of the stock clock speed on this thing, it's around 2500-2700 (on paper) and then there's a max boost clock of 3300. Stock settings on quiet mode, you're more likely to see around 2500-2600 (some times it won't even touch these numbers) but I peak around 3200 after toggling OC along with -40UV & +10% draw. I know what FSR and FG is, I also know about the Andrenalin functions. None of those settings were touched besides just toggling the bios switch on the physical card itself. 

Also to clarify a bit more on my quiet mode settings' performance, I used the following tweaks: +250 Frequency offset, -40 undervolt, 2718 memory timing, +10% power limit. Even with these settings I was only getting ~60fps in ultra settings 1440p Cyberpunk. Returned the settings to default then powered off pc > toggled OC > boot up and straight into game > ~100fps. The only tunings I did after were same the undervolt and power limit draw. It really was just that simple.

Yeston 16gb Gaming Ace OC paired with a 7700x if people are still wondering. Not a top tier setup but the gains were impressive to me as well as I was running it stock for the first week before toggling it. I don't gain anything from mentioning this method along with the proper procedure on how to toggle it on and off (only when pc is turned off).
